themes.label: Six enduring People Success needs
themes.summary: The framework organizes employee experience around purpose, growth, clarity, empowerment, connection, and wellbeing; it is a lens for listening and action, not six new AI intervention effects.

evidence.anchor: Purpose, Growth, Clarity, Empowerment, Connection and Wellbeing

themes.label: Meaningful work and observed voluntary exits
themes.summary: In the customer analysis, meaningful work was the highest-ranked voluntary-attrition correlate since 2022; favorable respondents were reported as 3.8 times less likely to leave. This is an observed comparison, not a validated individual forecast.

evidence.anchor: 3.8x less likely to leave

themes.label: Learning and career opportunities
themes.summary: Opportunities to learn and grow and good career opportunities were strongly associated with engagement outcomes. The reported learning/growth voluntary-exit comparison was 2.8 times lower among favorable respondents; career and growth are related but not identical items.

evidence.anchor: Opportunities to Learn and Grow

themes.label: Protected, role-relevant AI learning
themes.summary: Create time and psychological safety to experiment, with accessible resources, expert coaching, and manager guidance; prioritize targeted learning relevant to current work rather than simply adding broad training.

evidence.anchor: time to experiment and empathy

themes.label: Clarity about roles and priorities
themes.summary: Role expectations, priorities, and useful feedback were associated with observed voluntary exits. Employees who knew what to focus on were reported as 2.7 times less likely to leave; managers should clarify priorities during change rather than treat AI-generated task lists as sufficient.

evidence.anchor: 2.7x less likely to leave

themes.label: Performance feedback remains a human manager role
themes.summary: Performance feedback was the strongest reported correlate of satisfaction with one's manager over three years. The article recommends retaining human coaching and developing managers' feedback skill even when AI can assist.

evidence.anchor: the #1 driver of satisfaction

themes.label: Resources and permission to improve work
themes.summary: Resources and continuous process improvement correlated strongly with engagement; encouragement to find better ways of working had become especially strongly associated with satisfaction, recommendation, and belonging.

evidence.anchor: Encouraged to Try New Ways

themes.label: Use AI capacity for meaningful rather than more menial work
themes.summary: The author recommends directing time freed by AI toward higher-value, meaningful contributions and using job-specific scenarios and prompts to make empowerment practical. These are proposed applications, not effects tested in the customer attrition analysis.

evidence.anchor: higher value work

themes.label: Belonging as a retention-related experience
themes.summary: Belonging consistently ranked among the top five correlates of stated retention and observed voluntary attrition over three years. Connection includes collaboration, inclusion, feeling valued, and being accepted as oneself.

evidence.anchor: one of the top five drivers

themes.label: Accessible AI support for inclusion
themes.summary: The article proposes transcription, summarization, and communication assistance as ways AI may support different communication needs and neurodiverse colleagues. These use cases are recommendations, not new inclusion-effect estimates from the customer study.

evidence.anchor: supporting neurodiverse employees

themes.label: Care, support, and balance gained salience
themes.summary: Feeling cared for, supported, and able to balance work and life became more strongly associated with engagement and voluntary attrition after 2023. The article reports a 14% uptick in work-life balance's attrition-related importance since 2024, not a 14% change in exit rates.

evidence.anchor: largest uptick (14%)

themes.label: Communicate AI plans and invite concerns
themes.summary: Explain why AI is being implemented, its intended benefits, and employee-data protections; build psychological safety so employees can raise concerns. The article's proposed burnout analytics and assistants are not validated individual-risk models in this study.

evidence.anchor: how employee data will be protected

themes.label: Engagement analysis uses averaged customer correlations
themes.summary: The methods describe Pearson correlations between 25 critical-needs items and six engagement outcomes, averaged across customers within each reported year. Trend emphasis selects the top third of correlation changes; reported drivers are associations, not causal levers.

evidence.anchor: correlation strength of the linear relationship

themes.label: Attrition comparisons have a narrower eligible sample
themes.summary: Voluntary-exit analyses required at least 15 customers with at least 80 voluntary terminations between surveys, comparing favorable and unfavorable responses and averaging item multipliers at customer level. This is narrower than the headline millions of survey responses.

evidence.anchor: at least 80 voluntary terminations

themes.summary: The automated process produces aggregated benchmark scores without People Science directly viewing customer data. The release explicitly states that switching to eyes-off processing did not change calculations.

themes.summary: The release describes twice-yearly global and high-performing norms and annual industry/country norms using a rolling 12-month window; some specialty suites may need 24 months for coverage.

evidence.anchor: refreshed twice a year

themes.label: Coverage depends on item use

evidence.anchor: strict usage threshold

themes.label: Check the comparator and its vintage in reports

evidence.anchor: identified by name/year

themes.label: Small 2025 score movements are descriptive

themes.summary: Customer opt-outs and changes in item utilization can alter which organizations contribute each item's norm. These are offered as possible explanations for shifts, not tested causal decompositions.

themes.label: Migration pause broke the usual overlapping windows
themes.summary: The December 2024 refresh pause means July 2024–June 2025 data were compared with April 2023–March 2024, not the customary six-month-overlapping annual windows. Interpret that release comparison accordingly.

evidence.anchor: paused the regular refresh in December 2024

themes.label: Speaking up without interpersonal punishment
themes.summary: Psychological safety is a shared understanding that people may take risks, ask questions, voice concerns, and admit errors without embarrassment, rejection, or other negative consequences.

evidence.anchor: without fear of negative consequences

themes.summary: The article cites the 2024 APA Work in America survey: lower-safety employees were four times as likely to indicate wanting to quit, and 31% said they were not motivated to do their best work. themes.summary: Notice activation, pause to reflect, and ask curious follow-up questions rather than taking feedback personally. Defensive shutdown can teach employees not to speak; the article recommends self-awareness and respectful responses.

themes.label: Listen to understand rather than immediately solve
themes.summary: Listen with empathy and curiosity without imposing an agenda, controlling the conversation, explaining away concerns, or assuming every disclosure needs immediate problem-solving.

themes.label: Model vulnerability instead of declaring trust
themes.summary: Trust develops over time when leaders admit mistakes, share learning, and respond constructively to others' risk-taking; simply calling oneself a safe manager does not create immediate transparency.

themes.label: Recognize collaboration, candor, and belonging

themes.label: Build trust through recurring human check-ins

evidence.anchor: scheduling regular check-ins

themes.label: Honor the risk employees take in speaking up

evidence.anchor: thank them for sharing
